references.text: Pharaoh repeats his accusation that the Israelites are lazy (נִרְפִּים), using this as justification to refuse them permission to go and sacrifice to the Lord.
God instructed Moses to ask for permission to travel three days into the wilderness to sacrifice to the Lord, which Pharaoh here dismisses as an excuse.
Moses and Aaron first asked Pharaoh to let the people go to hold a festival for the Lord, which Pharaoh now calls laziness.
Moses and Aaron repeated their request to sacrifice (נִזְבְּחָה) to the Lord, using the same word that Pharaoh mocks them for here.
Proverbs warns against laziness (רָפָה), from the same root as נִרְפִּים, which Pharaoh uses to accuse the Israelites of being lazy.
Direct response in the same dialogue; Moses' demand for sacrificial journeys (v. 25) is the direct opposite of Pharaoh's accusation of laziness (v. 17).
